prerequisites: Prior knowledge of the contents of mechanics and strength of materials courses is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and ability to apply the fundamentals of elasticity and strength of materials to the behavior of real solids.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of industrial structures and constructions.
Understanding and mastery of basic concepts about the general laws of mechanics, thermodynamics, fields and waves, and electromagnetism and their application to solving engineering problems.
Knowledge and application of the principles of strength of materials.
Quantify stresses and deformations produced by a general bending state.
Quantify stresses and deformations produced by a torsion state in simple resistant elements.
Apply the principle of virtual works to different structural solids.
Apply the finite element method and matrix calculation to obtain stresses and deformations in different structural solids.

teaching_methods: Autonomous and group work (Self-study and group projects)

assessment_methods.method: Theoretical assessment (partial exams P1, P2, or final theoretical exam PF)

assessment_rules: In the ordinary call, the theoretical qualification (CT) is the average of P1 and P2, or the PF grade. A minimum of 4 out of 10 is required for P1, P2, and PF. The final grade is calculated as (0.6 x CT) + (0.15 x P3) + (0.11 x P4) + (0.07 x T1) + (0.07 x P5) if all minimums are met; otherwise, it's the minimum of this formula's result and CT. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is calculated as 0.6 x PF + (0.15 x P3) + (0.11 x P4) + (0.07 x T1) + (0.07 x P5), with a minimum of 4 out of 10 for PF. For differentiated evaluation, the final grade is 0.8 x PF + 0.2 x PP (Practical Exam).
